transcript.text:
Good morning, everyone. I've called us together because we have a time-sensitive matter to resolve. As you're all aware, the company discovered unauthorized access to a customer-facing system, and the incident-response team has completed its initial review. Our board's regular meeting is tomorrow, and the company wants any required public filing approved before that meeting. Currently, there is no SEC Form 8-K drafted for this incident on our filing calendar.

Under our normal pre-filing process, I need a final recommendation from each of you — cybersecurity, privacy, and investor-relations — before I can authorize an external filing. I'll settle the filing decision after I've received all three recommendations, without another round of questions.

I'd also note that the existing draft communications use general language about an investigation and do not specify the incident's regulatory classification, affected-account count, detailed operational impact, or ransom-demand treatment. Our board-approved communications process requires the final filing package to include a clear operational-continuity statement, omit ransom-demand details, and document a board review before filing authorization.

So let's work through this. I'd like to hear from each of you — what is your recommendation regarding whether we need to file an 8-K, and if so, what should the filing package contain?
